children: Analysis suggests Bitcoin could face large-scale short liquidations in the futures market.

On Nov. 21, on-chain analyst Darkfost wrote on X, formerly Twitter, that more than $2.4 billion in positions were liquidated across the digital-asset market over the past 24 hours. Of that total, 92.5% were long positions.
Most of the long positions built up over the past year have effectively been wiped out, he added. Potential long liquidations remaining near current price levels amount to only about $1 billion.

Darkfost highlighted that most positions still left in the futures market are short bets. If Bitcoin rises, about $23.5 billion in short positions could be liquidated, roughly 23.5 times the potential liquidation size for long positions, he wrote.

With short positions piled up to that extent, a rebound in Bitcoin could trigger a chain of forced liquidations. As those short positions are unwound, the resulting buy orders could fuel further gains and potentially lead to a short squeeze.

title: [Analysis] Bitcoin Futures Market Faces Risk of Mass Short Liquidations
